clue.text: Seduced, leader of team? Gutted, I must leave

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of team

indicators.note: the word I must leave the synonym, so that single letter is dropped from it

parts.note: a gutted fish or building has been emptied
taken as written, the letter that leaves

explanation.surface: A team captain, lured away and devastated, has to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' looks like British slang for bitterly disappointed, but it means emptied out; the 'I' of the clue is the letter that leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tempted is to be enticed or lured, which is the past-participle sense of seduced.

clue.text: Lot H? A Scott novel

parts.note: surface reading: a lot number at an auction, with a query
setter's reading: the four central letters of a Scottish county name spell these letters, and the title of a Walter Scott book describes exactly that

explanation.walkthrough: MIDLOTHIAN has ten letters; its middle four, its heart, are L-O-T-H. So 'Lot H' is literally the heart of Midlothian, which is also Scott's 1818 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Heart of Midlothian is a historical novel by Sir Walter Scott, named after Edinburgh's old Tolbooth prison.

clue.text: See 1
Heavy blow to rear with end of cane or strap

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing up means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a swat is a hard smack

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: last letter of cane

explanation.surface: A description of corporal punishment: a hard smack on the backside with a cane or a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces. A TAWSE is a leather strap with split ends once used to punish Scottish schoolchildren, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The tawse is a Scottish leather strap, formerly used for punishment in schools.

clue.text: River pilot's first view, reportedly, of distant waters

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England

indicators.note: the pilot's first is the opening letter of that word

parts.note: first letter of pilot

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so we want a word pronounced the same as the synonym

parts.note: to view is to see, which is pronounced like the word for the ocean

explanation.surface: A river pilot gets a first glimpse of faraway waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-sea describes the open ocean far from shore, so it suits waters that are distant from land.

clue.text: Weigh down with work at mill

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a press is a machine for crushing, as a mill is; 'at mill' is the thing working there

explanation.surface: A worker in a mill is burdened by toil.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is the usual crossword abbreviation for opus, a musical work; a press, like a mill, squeezes or crushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to burden someone heavily, just as being weighed down means bearing a heavy load.

clue.text: Old copper's bagging best fairground ride

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: bagging means capturing and holding inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive
top means the best

explanation.surface: An elderly policeman is capturing the best ride at the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, Cu; TOP slips in between its C and U.
explanation.definitionFit: The octopus is a fairground ride whose cars spin on the ends of several long arms, like tentacles.

clue.text: Phone, by special arrangement, one pursued by spies in ancient land

indicators.note: something pursued by another goes in front, so the second piece follows the first
a special arrangement of letters means they are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Arrange a telephone call specially, with someone tailed by secret agents in an old country.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was an ancient civilisation on the coast of the Levant, in present-day Lebanon.

clue.text: Marathon record I start to challenge

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all we keep

parts.note: first letter of challenge

explanation.surface: A runner sets out to challenge a marathon record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marathon' looks like a race, but here it is an adjective meaning very long.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon session is very long and arduous, and epic likewise describes something huge in length or scale.

clue.text: Extremely stark, the old island

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two outermost letters

parts.note: outer letters of stark
ye is an old spelling of the

explanation.surface: The bleak old isle is very stark.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Special wine — comply with note about date aand it should mature in time

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around another
special suggests something specially made up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
D is an abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A sommelier's note on a special wine that should age well over time.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine surface makes 'mature' sound like ageing in the bottle; the definition is about money. 'aand' is a misprint of 'and' in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment policy is a life insurance savings plan that pays out a lump sum when it matures at the end of a fixed term.

clue.text: Call up? That's all right during late part of day

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: evening, the late part of the day
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A late-evening phone call: is it all right to ring?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' looks like telephoning; here it means bringing to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory is to summon it into the mind, which is calling it up.

clue.text: Lying down in middle of bed after drink

indicators.note: the earlier words come after the drink, so the drink is placed first

parts.note: to sup is to drink
taken as written

indicators.note: the middle of a three-letter word is its single central letter

parts.note: middle letter of bed

explanation.surface: Someone lies in the middle of the bed after a nightcap.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on the back, face upward, which is one way of lying down.

clue.text: Bob and William typed up 'Seals at Sea — Aquatic Mammals'

parts.note: to bob is to dip down quickly, to duck

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: Bill is short for William
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two men, Bob and William, typed up a magazine headline about seals and other sea mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob and William look like typists, but they become DUCK and BILL; the anagram of the next three words supplies the ED as well as the platypuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Platypuses are egg-laying Australian mammals that hunt underwater in rivers and streams.

clue.text: See 12
Tramp breaking lots of wine bottles

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: reams means lots, as in reams of paper
a hobo is a tramp

explanation.surface: A vagrant smashes a pile of wine bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is a large wine or champagne bottle holding six standard bottles, named after a biblical king.

clue.text: One may be heading for a port abattoir (strange name)

definitions.text: One may be heading for a port

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are in an odd, unnatural order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
N is an abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Livestock may be heading for an abattoir at a port, one with an odd name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a port abattoir' sounds like the destination of animals; the definition is the opening words only.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat train runs to a harbour to connect with a ferry or ship, so it heads for a port.

clue.text: Painful ulcer needs treatment

indicators.note: treatment works something over, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sore ulcer needs medical attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel can mean causing pain or distress, as in a cruel blow, so it is a synonym of painful.

clue.text: Port in Japan, very large, known by another name as well?

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, a clothing size

parts.words: known by another name as well?
parts.note: aka stands for also known as

explanation.surface: Is this big Japanese port also called by another name?
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major city and seaport on the Japanese island of Honshu.

clue.text: Additional demand in racing town

parts.note: new can mean additional, as in a new supply
a market for goods is the demand for them

explanation.surface: A fresh levy is imposed in a town known for horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket in Suffolk is the headquarters of British horse racing, with famous courses and training stables.

clue.text: Not settled in the Channel Islands, boy's upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom up

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
Damon is a boy's name; the 's makes it 'boy is'

explanation.surface: A lad who has never settled in the Channel Islands is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British islands off Normandy, Jersey and Guernsey among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people move from place to place rather than living in one settled home.

clue.text: US breakdown vehicle crew crashed by roadside? Almost

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other
something crashed is wrecked and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: the kerb is the edge of the pavement beside the road

explanation.surface: An American tow truck's crew crashed by the side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerb is the British spelling of curb, the raised edge of a pavement. The surface fits nicely: a wrecker is what would come to a roadside crash.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a wrecker is a tow truck used to haul away broken-down or crashed vehicles.

clue.text: Awfully misty approaching end of office block

indicators.note: approaching means coming up to, so the first piece comes just before the second
awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter alone

parts.note: last letter of office

explanation.surface: It is very foggy near the far end of the office block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office block' reads as a building; 'block' alone is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart someone's plans, which is to block them.

clue.text: Strong and wiry copper arresting teacher in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the whole is read backwards
arresting someone means holding them, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a PC, police constable, is a copper
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A tough, wiry policeman arrests a retired schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' here is the policeman (PC), unlike in 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp hair is firm and springy, and crisp also means firm and brisk, close to strong and wiry.

clue.text: Supply food for social event in Surrey town (not meat)

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word is removed

parts.note: Caterham is a town in Surrey
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: Feeding guests at a party in a Surrey town, with a vegetarian menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south of London. Remove HAM from the end of CATERHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Caterers provide the meals and refreshments for parties, weddings and other functions.

clue.text: A British graduate in pop group

parts.note: taken as written
B is an abbreviation for British
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A British university graduate plays in a band.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA was the Swedish band that won Eurovision in 1974 and had many pop hits.

clue.text: Join up, then fall heavily

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to meet is to join, as roads meet

explanation.surface: Enlist, then come down hard: a soldier's lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join up' reads as enlisting; here 'up' turns the synonym over.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that teems pours down in torrents, so it falls heavily.

clue.text: Like street bands playing for amusement

indicators.note: playing with something means moving it around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Buskers performing in the street to entertain people.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is a pub game like ninepins; the phrase is usually used in the negative, as in 'life isn't all beer and skittles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer and skittles stands for pleasure and leisure, so it is an idiom for amusement.

clue.text: Yearbook bound by local man, a collector

indicators.note: bound by means held inside the following words, so the letters run across them

parts.note: runs across the end of local, man, a and the start of collector

explanation.surface: An annual is bound by a man from the area who collects things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' suggests book-binding, which suits the yearbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual publication of calendars, tables and facts, so it is a yearbook.

clue.text: New rose-red screen

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters are made into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new screen in a rosy red colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or panel behind a church altar.
